chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ali bin Mahziyar, from Muhammad bin Al-Hasan Al-Ash'ari, who said:

One of our companions wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second, along with me, asking him about a man who was immoral with a woman, then he married her after the pregnancy, so she came with a child, and he resembled him the most from the creatures of Allah. So he wrote by his handwriting and his seal: 'The child of sin does not inherit'.

key_terms.فَجَرَ: To be immoral or commit illicit intercourse

ai.seo_question: Does a child inherit from the father if he married the mother after the pregnancy resulting from illicit intercourse?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi records Imam al-Ja'far al-Sadiq's (AS) specific ruling that the child of illicit intercourse remains 'for sin' (li-ghayyah) and does not inherit from the father, even if the man subsequently marries the mother. This highlights the Shia juristic distinction between the validity of marriage and the attribution of lineage, emphasizing that the 'fujur' (illicit act) creates a permanent barrier to inheritance rights regardless of later marital union.
